rule.words: We NEED to have the same or better optionally than V6. We MUST offer as many steps and tapers as V6! ... In general - optional it must be at least v6. We must have Gogo, goslow and nogo years.

summary: One row for every thing a person can see, set or press in today's app, and for every key it saves. The rows started from section 4 of the square-one audit (research/v7/square-one-audit.md) and were completed from the code: the test reads every key today's app saves straight from the code and the twelve test plans, so a new key fails the test until it has a row here.

**Built** means the /v7/ preview offers it, named by file. **Building now** marks work under way (none at present: the spending shape's steps and tapers are built, and its other parts are designed). **Designed** names the V7 document and section. **Planned** names the step that delivers it; "no V7 design yet" marks the ones no V7 document gives a place, which by the owner's rule stay unless the owner retires them. **Retired** gives the release-note reason; a retired option waits for the owner.

Where only part of a thing is in V7, the row is split (the part V7 has is built, the rest planned) or its note says what is missing. Line numbers are today's working copy (6.20.2) and will drift; the names beside them are the lasting reference. The spending shape's rows were checked in a browser on 2 Oct 2026, at 390 and 1280 px, beside today's planner's editor (guest only); the other rows' V7 files were read, not exercised.

The test holds every row built or designed, none retired, and none waiting on a thing with no V7 design.

rows.name: Landing page, welcome tour and set-up wizard
rows.what: Shows a new person what the app does, then asks name, single or couple, ages and retirement age, and where to start: work out my budget, can I afford to retire, this month's withdrawal, or I'm already drawing.
rows.note: Replaced by the six questions in the person's own words. The wizard's "I'm already drawing" door is question D (step s7-d).

rows.name: Try it without an account
rows.what: Lets a visitor see answers before signing up.
rows.note: Better: V7 answers on the visitor's own figures with no account; what was typed stays in the tab.

rows.name: A ready-made example plan
rows.what: Opens a worked example plan (about £1m, already retired) to look around every tool before typing anything.
rows.whereV6: Guest example plan and the ?demo=1m link (index.html:5036-5084)
rows.note: V7's answers on your own figures are the new way in; an example to look around has no V7 home yet.

rows.name: Guest mode: three active hours, reminders, then hand-over into an account
rows.what: A visitor can build a whole plan without an account for three active hours, is reminded as time runs out, and keeps the plan when they sign up.
rows.whereV6: GuestMeter.js; the guest store in FirestoreService.js; the guest banner (index.html)
rows.note: V7's answers do not count against the three hours; the audit recommends keeping that and recording it (square-one-audit.md §6 question 5). The meter itself needs a place in V7's shell.

rows.name: Next-step banner
rows.what: One sentence at the top saying what to do next for this plan, with a button, dismissable per plan.
rows.note: The rail's "next" sentence, by question and by stage (also §1.4).

rows.name: Life stages lead the way
rows.what: Works out from dates whether the plan is saving, approaching, committed while saving, retired in its run-up or running, and opens the right tool for it.
rows.whereV6: LifeStage.js deriveStage; tabs led by stage (index.html:8866-8870)
rows.note: Stages in V7's words, and which questions each stage is offered (§1.5 table). Needs V7 to open a saved plan.

rows.name: Journey: when the plan moved between stages
rows.what: Keeps the dates on which the plan's stage changed (saving, approaching, committed, running).
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: Finding your way on a phone
rows.what: A bottom bar (Budget, Stress, Strategies, Decide) and a More menu for the other tabs.
rows.note: The rail is one line under the header that opens as a sheet. The locked plan's rail on a phone is designed (rail-screens-language.md §1.7).

rows.name: Open today's app on a given tab
rows.what: A one-off note in the tab that tells today's app which tab to open next (used when another page sends someone in).
rows.note: "Change this" on V7's plan rail opens today's tool on the right tab through it (square-one-audit.md §5 item 4).

rows.name: Spending lines
rows.what: Lists what you spend, line by line, each a month or a year, after tax, at today's prices; lines can be added, named and removed.
rows.whereV6: Budget tab: Essential and Lifestyle spending (index.html:3887-3953; BudgetModel.js)
rows.note: The budget step of A and B; a plan made from an answer carries the lines into the plan's Budget.

rows.name: Lines grouped by heading
rows.what: Groups lines under headings (home and bills, food, getting about, holidays, health, family and giving, other).
rows.whereV6: Walk-through groups (index.html BUD_WIZ_GROUPS); a heading carried from V7

rows.name: Essential or lifestyle, and the essentials total
rows.what: Marks each line essential or lifestyle and shows the essentials as their own total.
rows.note: In V7 the essentials total is for the person's own judgement; it never becomes a floor (owner, 1 Oct 2026).

rows.name: Typical UK amounts as hints
rows.what: Shows beside each line what a typical household spends on it, at the chosen national level.
rows.whereV6: Budget tab and walk-through "use this" chips (BudgetModel.typicalMonthlyFor)

rows.name: Fill the blanks with typical amounts
rows.what: One press fills every empty line with the typical UK amount, to edit from there.
rows.whereV6: Budget tab: "Fill blanks with typical UK amounts" (index.html:3911)
rows.note: budget-step.md shows typical amounts as hints only, never filled in. By the rule of 2 Oct the one-press fill stays unless the owner retires it.

rows.name: National guide levels
rows.what: Minimum, moderate and comfortable retirement spending for one or two people, to aim at or compare with.
rows.whereV6: Budget tab: "What are you aiming for?" (index.html:3888-3895)
rows.note: A guide beside the spending box, or the figure itself when picked.

rows.name: Guided walk-through
rows.what: Takes you through the budget category by category, with a tip for each (care costs, holidays in the early years, car replacement).
rows.note: V7's sheet covers the lines by heading on one page; the step-by-step walk-through with its tips has no V7 design.

rows.name: Break a line into sub-items
rows.what: A small calculator under a line: list the parts (e.g. each insurance), and their total becomes the line.

rows.name: Sums in the amount boxes
rows.what: An amount box takes a sum such as =200*12 or 1,200 and works it out.

rows.name: A line from or to an age
rows.what: A line can start or stop at an age, e.g. the mortgage ends at 63, or care costs from 85.
rows.note: D adds one later amount (answer-D.md §5.3); lines by age need E's spending section, alongside the spending shape.

rows.name: One-off and every-few-years costs
rows.what: Lists costs that come at an age or every few years (a car every 8 years, a roof).
rows.note: Shown as a guide beside the figure, not added to it (budget-step.md).

rows.name: Horizon: age today, retirement age, plan to age
rows.what: The three ages the budget is worked over; whether you have retired; when the age was given.
rows.note: V7 asks the ages once, in each question.

rows.name: Partner's age, retirement age, retired or not
rows.what: The partner's ages, kept on the budget for a couple.
rows.whereV6: Set-up wizard and Household → Create their plan (index.html:4900-4926, 10877-10887)
rows.note: V7 asks the partner's age and stop on the first screen (partnerStopFields).

rows.name: Who pays: me, partner or shared, and my share
rows.what: For a couple, each line and one-off is paid by me, my partner or shared, with my share as a percentage (budget-wide or per line).
rows.note: V7's budget is the household's (budget-step.md).

rows.name: Who pays, changing over time
rows.what: My share of shared costs can change at an age, e.g. 70% until her pension starts at 63, then 50/50.
rows.whereV6: Budget: "Change who pays over time" (index.html:3876-3880; BudgetModel.budgetSharePctAtAge)

rows.name: Headroom on top of the budget
rows.what: Adds a monthly margin on top of the budget's total when it becomes the plan's target.
rows.reason: The spending figure is now always your own, with the budget as a guide beside it (owner, 1 Oct 2026), so there is no budget total to add a margin to: type the figure with the margin you want.
rows.owner: to confirm (follows from the rule of 1 Oct 2026 that the budget is a guide; budget-step.md)

rows.name: Use the budget's total as the spending figure
rows.what: Copies the budget's total into the plan's spending figure.
rows.whereV6: Budget: "Use as the start of my income shape" (index.html:12172-12200; BudgetToPlan.js)
rows.note: Changed on purpose: one tap copies the total into the box and the person can change it; nothing else flows from the budget (owner, 1 Oct 2026). Today's button also writes the essentials into Floor & Flex.

rows.name: Export and import the budget as a spreadsheet
rows.what: Downloads the whole budget as a CSV that opens in Google Sheets or Excel, and reads an edited one back, with one undo.
rows.whereV6: Budget: Export CSV / Import CSV (index.html:3912-3913; BudgetModel.budgetToCsv, parseBudgetCsv)

rows.name: Did you miss anything?
rows.what: Suggests common costs not yet in the budget, one press to add each.

rows.name: A nudge when an amount looks wrong
rows.what: Flags an amount that is far below or far above what households typically spend on that line (a nudge, never a block).

rows.name: Reset, duplicate a line, undo a removal
rows.what: Start the budget again (ages kept), duplicate a line or one-off, and undo a line removed by mistake.

rows.name: The budget's version and stored totals
rows.what: A version mark, and the totals (essentials, comfortable, suggested gross) worked out again on every save.
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: Whether a line's panels were left open
rows.what: Whether a line's age band or breakdown was open on screen when it was saved.
rows.reason: Screen state saved with the line by accident, not a setting: V7 keeps open panels in the screen itself. Nothing a person set is lost.

rows.name: Steps by age: "from age X take £Y a year"
rows.what: The spending shape: each step is the total income wanted from an age on (State Pension, other pensions and the pot together), as many steps as wanted. One step is level for life.
rows.whereV6: Stress tester → Settings → Your income shape (index.html:3198-3215, 9118-9162; IncomeSchedule.js)
rows.note: A and B: on the spend step, under the figure, "Does what you spend change as you get older?" → "Change it with age": any number of steps by age (up to one a year of the plan), each a month after tax. C: the same block under "Add more detail", each step a share of what you start on. Each year's figure is today's own IncomeSchedule.amountAtAge (imported). A couple's ages are yours, with your partner's beside each step.

rows.name: Add a step, remove a step
rows.what: "+ Add a step" adds one ten years after the last and £10,000 lower; any step but the first can be removed. No limit on how many.
rows.note: "+ Add a step" adds one 10 years after the last and 10% lower (today: £10,000 a year lower), and puts the keyboard in its age box; "Remove the step from 75" on every step after the first. No limit but one a year of the plan.

rows.name: A taper within a step: falling by a real % a year
rows.what: Each step can fall each year by 0% to 5% in today's money, in quarter-point steps, compounding (£60,000 at 1% pays £59,400 the next year).
rows.whereV6: The slider on each step (index.html:9133-9136; IncomeSchedule.amountAtAge)
rows.note: Every step, the first included, "falls by …% a year": 0.25% to 10% in quarter points (today's slider stops at 5%), compounding at today's prices, by today's own amountAtAge.

rows.name: A taper to the next step: glide evenly
rows.what: Instead of a cliff, a step can walk down in a straight line to the next step's amount, arriving as that step starts.
rows.whereV6: "glide evenly to the next step" on each step (index.html:9137; IncomeSchedule.amountAtAge)
rows.note: "moves evenly to the next step" on every step but the last: a straight line in pounds arriving as the next step starts, by today's own amountAtAge.

rows.name: Go-go, go-slow and no-go years
rows.what: Explains the three phases of retirement spending, go-go (travel, projects, while fit), go-slow (from the mid-70s, typically drifting down 1-2% a year) and no-go (the basics, and care if it comes), and colours the years of the picture by phase (to 75, 75 to 85, 85 on).
rows.whereV6: Your income shape: the words above the steps and the bar colours (index.html:3199-3200; incomeShapeGraphic.js)
rows.note: The words above the steps name go-go (travel, projects), go-slow (from the mid-70s) and no-go (less again, though care can cost more); the picture draws the three bands at 75 and 85 (a couple: of the younger of you).

rows.name: Suggest go-slow and no-go steps
rows.what: One press adds suggested later steps from the first: 15% lower from 75 and 30% lower from 85, never below the budget's essentials, rounded to £500. Typical, not yours: edit freely.
rows.note: "Suggest go-go, go-slow and no-go years": today's suggestSteps in V7's units: 15% less from 75 and 30% less from 85, never below the budget's essentials, to the nearest £10 a month (today: £500 a year); for a couple, from when the younger of you is 75 and 85. Says what it filled in, and has Undo (today's has none). The preset "Slowly less" is today's old "declining with age" (smileToSteps).

rows.name: Start from my budget
rows.what: Sets the first step from the budget's total with tax added on.
rows.note: "Use £X a month" copies the budget's total into the figure (the budget stays a guide: owner, 1 Oct 2026); later steps are kept, as today, and "Move the later steps in proportion" is offered.

rows.name: Start from a number
rows.what: Sets the first step from a figure typed in.
rows.note: The figure box on the spend step is the first amount; "The same every year" clears the steps (today's "or a number" replaces them all).

rows.name: The staircase picture
rows.what: Draws the shape as a bar for each year of age, coloured by go-go, go-slow and no-go, with a line along the tops.
rows.note: A bar a year from the start to the end of the plan, at 390 px with no sideways scroll; tap or point at a bar to read that year; "Show each year" opens a table. The motion as the steps change is its own row (income.staircase-motion), not built.

rows.name: The picture moves from the old shape to the new one
rows.what: When a step changes, the bars ease from their old heights to the new ones (about half a second) instead of jumping.
rows.note: Not built: V7's picture jumps to the new shape. Designed: each bar scales from its old height to its new one, and not at all for anyone who has asked their device for less motion.

rows.name: State Pension and other income as layers
rows.what: Inside each year's bar: the State Pension from its date, other income and a final-salary pension, income streams for their years, and on top what the pot must supply.
rows.note: On the answer's picture (A, B and C): each year's bar has the State Pension and other pensions (and pay or part-time work) after tax drawn lighter, and what the pension and savings pay darker, from the answer's own year-by-year rows. The same layers while the steps are set (income.layers-editing), the budget's total (income.budget-mark) and the markers for lump sums and one-off spends (income.markers) are rows of their own, not built.

rows.name: The layers while you set the steps
rows.what: As the steps are set, before any test is run, the picture already shows the State Pension and other income inside each bar, and what the pot must supply on top.
rows.note: Not built: the spend step's picture shows the shape alone ("Each bar is one year of your life"); the layers come with the answer. Designed: the spend step reads the year-by-year income you get anyway from the plan the inputs already make (yearsOf, no engine run), once a stop age is known.

rows.name: The budget's total marked on the picture
rows.what: A short line at the left of the picture marks the budget's total (with tax added), so the first step can be read against it.
rows.note: Not built as a mark: V7 says it in words beside each later step ("85% of the start, 71% of your budget (a guide)"). Designed: a short dashed mark at the budget's total a month, named in the key, a guide only.

rows.name: Lump sums and one-off spends marked at their ages
rows.what: A lump sum arriving (▲) and a one-off spend (▼, with its years) are drawn on the picture at their ages, with their amounts.
rows.note: Waits for one-off costs (§16) and lump sums (§17), which V7 does not have yet. Designed: a mark under the bar of that year, its amount in the year's line and in the table.

rows.name: Below the essentials turns orange
rows.what: The budget's essentials are a line on the picture; a step below them turns orange and a note says the floor strategies will not buy less than the bills.
rows.note: With a budget: the essentials are a dashed line, a year below them is marked in the warning colour, and a note says so in words ("That is allowed: it is your figure"). A guide only: never a floor (owner, 1 Oct 2026).

rows.name: Never below guaranteed income
rows.what: A year whose step would fall below the income that arrives anyway (State Pension, other pensions) is held there, with a note from which age.
rows.note: The engine takes nothing from the pots in a year whose State Pension and other pensions (after tax) pay more than the step; the answer's note "shape-below-income" says from which age, and the picture shows that year's bar as the income itself. Today's editor also says it while the steps are set: that is its own row (income.below-income-live), not built.

rows.name: "Below the income you get anyway", said while setting the steps
rows.what: While the steps are set, an orange note says from which age a step is below the income that arrives anyway (State Pension, other pensions), which then pays instead.
rows.note: Not built: V7 says it on the answer only. Designed: the same words on the spend step, from the same year-by-year income as the layers (§15.1).

rows.name: Each later step as a share of the budget
rows.what: Beside each later step: its amount as a % of the budget (or of "your budget (a guide)" on a plan made from a V7 answer).
rows.note: Beside each later step: "85% of the start", and with a budget "85% of the start, 71% of your budget (a guide)", as today's "— 85% of today's budget".

rows.name: The first step's take-home a month
rows.what: Says what the first step leaves a month after tax at today's bands.
rows.note: Not needed as a separate line: every V7 figure is typed and shown after tax, a month (today's line turns its before-tax step into take-home). The answer's "what it is made of" shows the tax.

rows.name: Turn a lump sum into income
rows.what: For each lump sum: what it could add a year if spread over the years left, and one press to add that to the steps from its age (the lump stays as the money that pays for it).
rows.note: Waits for lump sums (inc.lump-sums, designed in spending-shape.md §17). Then "Turn it into income" gives what the lump sum could add a month over the years left, after tax, and one tap raises the step in force at its age and every later one by that (raiseFrom(age, a month): today's "Add £X/yr to my income from 67", spending-shape.md §2 T16). The test of it is marked to-do (tests/v7/screens/shapeParity.test.js T16).

rows.name: Extra spends in a given year
rows.what: A car, a roof, a wedding: an amount drawn on top of the income shape in a plan year (or several), taxed like income, which every strategy must fund.
rows.whereV6: Income streams & lump sums: + Extra spend (index.html:10636-10637)
rows.note: Not built. Designed inside the spending shape: "Any one-off costs?" under the steps (A, B, D; C under "Add more detail"): an amount after tax at an age, once or every year for a number of years, going up with prices or a fixed sum, with a name. Each year's need is the shape's figure plus that year's costs; kept plans get today's extraWithdrawals, exact to the year. The budget's one-off costs stay a guide: one tap copies them.

rows.name: The year-by-year figure every tool reads
rows.what: The shape compiled to one figure a year from the plan's start age, read by every strategy, the stress tests and the Decision tool; the first step is the Decision tool's target.
rows.note: Every V7 answer (C, A, B) works out each year's figure from the shape and tests it year by year. "Save this as a plan" writes seed version 3 for a shaped answer, and today's planner turns it into its own income steps (compressSteps) that give the answer's after-tax figure in every year, to the pound.

rows.name: Amounts before tax, in today's money
rows.what: Every step is £ a year before tax at today's prices; tax comes out of it.
rows.note: V7 asks after tax, a month (square-one-audit.md §5); the kept plan carries today's before-tax, a-year steps, each year grossed up by today's own grossUpAnnual, so both readings hold.

rows.name: What you want to spend, take-home, a month or a year
rows.what: The spending need typed as take-home, a month or a year, with the gross worked out and a chip to use the budget's figure.
rows.whereV6: Decision tool → Settings → Spending need (index.html:2553-2575); the hidden Stress box
rows.note: One figure a month after tax, or a national level. Today's box also takes the figure a year; V7 asks a month only.

rows.name: Age today
rows.what: Your age now, dated, which with the State Pension date pins every plan year to a tax year and an age.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → When your plan starts (index.html:3150-3166)
rows.note: Asked in every question.

rows.name: Retired already, or retiring at an age
rows.what: "I have already retired" or "I will retire at age X".
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → When your plan starts (index.html:3153-3154)
rows.note: A and B ask the stop age (or "I've already stopped"); C asks when the money starts.

rows.name: Plan starts this tax year or next April
rows.what: Which tax year is the plan's year 0; months before it are bridge months, lived on cash.
rows.note: square-one-audit.md §5: offer "I've stopped; my plan's income starts next April" as a plain choice.

rows.name: Pots at retirement, projected
rows.what: For someone still working, projects the pots to the retirement age from today's pots and payments.
rows.whereV6: When your plan starts: the projection line (index.html:8953-8957)
rows.note: Better: the saving-years engine gives a middling and a bad case.

rows.name: Pots at retirement, typed in
rows.what: Overrides the projection with the pension and ISA you expect to have on the day, in today's money.
rows.whereV6: When your plan starts: "Or SIPP at retirement", "ISA at retirement" (index.html:3160-3161)
rows.note: A plan made from a V7 answer writes the middling pot here (PlanSeed.js); no V7 form lets the person type it.

rows.name: How long the plan runs
rows.what: The plan's length in years (the age it runs to).
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → Duration; Decision → Depletion Duration
rows.note: Asked as the age to plan to (endAge, 75 to 105, 95 by default).

rows.name: Suggest a plan length from longevity
rows.what: Suggests the length from age and sex: a 1-in-10 chance of living beyond (cautious), 1 in 4, or average.

rows.name: "Update this draft to today"
rows.what: A draft whose start year has passed is offered an update to today; "Leave it" is remembered.

rows.name: Pension pot, split into shares, bonds and cash
rows.what: The pension total and how it splits into the three pots the plan draws from; their floors run down over the plan (the glidepath).
rows.whereV6: Stress and Decision → Settings → Your allocation (index.html:3329-3333)
rows.note: V7 asks the pension total; the split follows the risk level.

rows.name: Risk level: cautious, balanced, adventurous
rows.what: Sets the mix of shares, bonds and cash, or switches to testing a list of funds.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: Pick a risk level / Test on a list of funds (index.html:3303-3306, 3379-3393)
rows.note: V7 has a risk level while drawing and another while saving.

rows.name: Test on a list of funds
rows.what: A list of funds, each tagged to a bucket and a sub-class (searched, typed or pasted from a platform), becomes the allocation the plan is tested on. Each strategy keeps its own list.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation → Test on a list of funds (index.html:3407-3430; PortfolioTagger.js, FundCatalogue.js)
rows.note: E's "mix" step: a pot and a risk level; a fund list there is the intended retirement portfolio.

rows.name: An example ETF portfolio for the risk level
rows.what: Shows an illustrative fund portfolio for the chosen level (not advice).
rows.whereV6: "See an example ETF portfolio for this level" (index.html:3398-3401; ModelPortfolios.js)

rows.name: Diversifiers sleeve: gold and trend/macro
rows.what: Carves a slice into assets that tend to hold up when shares fall, held flat and sold first in a downturn; the target rises with prices and runs down like the others.

rows.name: Bond tent
rows.what: Shares rise over time: bond-heavy early, when the pot is largest and most exposed to an early crash, share-heavy later, centred on the risk level; a tagged plan sets its end mix.

rows.name: ISA (and savings) total
rows.what: The ISA held beside the pension, drawn as its own pot.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: Total in your ISA (index.html:3335)
rows.note: Asked as savings (ISAs and other savings).

rows.name: How the ISA is used
rows.what: Tax-efficient (tops up income before higher-rate tax), make it last to the State Pension, or hold it (never drawn for income; it still rescues a plan whose pension runs out).
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: How the ISA is used (index.html:3337-3343)

rows.name: How the ISA and savings grow, and the ISA's floor
rows.what: One choice per plan: "Mostly cash" (the default; like the pension's cash, last year's rise in prices less 1%, never below nothing) or "Invested like my pension" (the pension's mix of shares, bonds and cash, in the same futures). A plan locked before the choice keeps a fixed 3% a year (isaReturn) until it is unlocked. Also the floor the ISA is drawn down towards (isaMin).
rows.whereV6: Stress tester → Settings → How your ISA and savings grow (index.html #ssIsaGrowthGroup; src/ui/isaGrowthSetting.js, src/services/IsaGrowth.js); the floor in the settings defaults (constants.js ISA_DEFAULTS)
rows.note: One choice under the savings box in C, A and B ("Mostly cash" or "Invested like my pension"), carried between them and into a plan made from the answer; today's planner has the same choice in Stress tester → Settings from 6.22.0 (schema version 3 writes "Mostly cash" into every unlocked plan). The floor (isaMin) is saved but read by no engine in either app: both draw the ISA down to nothing.

rows.name: A taxable account (GIA)
rows.what: Money held outside a pension or ISA: how much, what it holds (shares, gilts, bond funds, a mix, cash) and the tax band it is taxed at; it is drawn first and taxed each year.
rows.whereV6: Your allocation: Taxable investments today (index.html:3347-3376; TaxableSleeve.js)
rows.note: answer-D.md §9.2 reads the ordinary account from a locked plan's holdings; no V7 form asks for it.

rows.name: Charges (funds and platform), % a year
rows.what: One charge a year taken off monthly from funds and cash, while saving and while drawing.

rows.name: State Pension amount
rows.what: The State Pension from the forecast: full, a forecast amount, or none.
rows.whereV6: Stress and Decision → Settings → State Pension (index.html:3546-3561)

rows.name: State Pension start date, typed from the forecast
rows.what: The exact date it starts, as on the forecast (also the birthday the plan reckons ages from).
rows.note: V7 works the date out from age (schemaParts.statePensionAgeOf) and does not ask it.

rows.name: The old State Pension fields
rows.what: The State Pension as an annual figure from a plan year, from before the start date was asked; read only when a plan has no date.
rows.note: V7 must read an old plan the same way (fallback only, never asked).

rows.name: Final-salary pension: amount and start
rows.what: A defined-benefit pension: how much a year, in today's money, and when it starts.
rows.whereV6: Other income: Defined-Benefit Pension, DB Starts as a plan year (index.html:3508-3534)
rows.note: Better: V7 asks the start by age, not plan year, for each person.

rows.name: How a final-salary pension rises
rows.what: Rises with prices capped at 5%, with full prices, or not at all.
rows.note: V7's household takes all three (household.js) but the forms always say prices capped at 5%.

rows.name: Other income or pension
rows.what: Another taxable income a year from now, rising with prices capped at 4%.
rows.note: D designs income you have bought (answer-D.md §5.2); a general other income has no V7 form.

rows.name: Part-time work for some years
rows.what: Earnings for a number of years after stopping.
rows.note: A's "Would some part-time work help?"; D designs the same for the retired (answer-D.md §3.6).

rows.name: Income for some years
rows.what: Any taxable income between two plan years (rent that ends, part-time work, a small pension), with how it rises.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → Income streams & lump sums (index.html:3535-3545, 10635-10641)
rows.note: Only part-time work from the stop is asked in V7 (row above).

rows.name: One-off lump sums
rows.what: Money arriving in a plan year (an inheritance, downsizing): where it can legally go (ISA allowance, pension up to earnings or the £10,000 limit, the rest taxable), what it is held in, and the Decision tool's advice in its year.
rows.whereV6: Income streams & lump sums: + One-off lump sum (index.html:10639-10660; TaxableSleeve.routeWindfall)
rows.note: Not built. Designed: "Money you expect to come in" on the pots step (A, B; C under "Add more detail"): an amount at an age, and what it is (cash, an inherited pension, an inherited ISA). Where it can go is today's own routeWindfall (the ISA allowance, the pension within its limit, the rest a taxable account); kept plans get today's windfalls.

rows.name: Tax thresholds
rows.what: Personal allowance, basic-rate limit and higher-rate limit for year 0, which can be changed.
rows.note: V7 uses today's bands (toEngine.js BANDS) and they cannot be changed.

rows.name: Thresholds rise with prices, or stay frozen
rows.what: Whether the tax bands rise with inflation or stay where they are.

rows.name: The 25% tax-free part: in each withdrawal, or kept separate
rows.what: Take a quarter of every withdrawal tax-free (UFPLS), or count every withdrawal as taxable because the tax-free sum is taken or kept for something else.
rows.note: V7 takes a quarter of each withdrawal tax-free unless you say it is already taken.

rows.name: Tax-free part for some years, then the rest into the ISA
rows.what: Take the tax-free quarter for a number of years, then move the remaining 25% into the ISA before switching to drawdown.
rows.whereV6: How you'll take this pension: UFPLS for how many years (index.html:3002-3014)
rows.note: F's "tax-free cash and which pot first" is the decision page (rail-screens-language.md §1.5); the plan's own setting needs E.

rows.name: Fill the basic-rate band and recycle into the ISA
rows.what: Draws extra pension up to the 20% band even when spending does not need it, and moves the net into the ISA (up to £20,000 a year).
rows.whereV6: How you'll take this pension: band fill (index.html:3016-3025)
rows.note: No test plan uses it yet (square-one-audit.md §4).

rows.name: Bed-and-ISA £20,000 a year
rows.what: Moves £20,000 a year from the taxable account into the ISA whenever the allowance is unused.

rows.name: Relevant UK earnings
rows.what: Earnings this year, which set how much of a lump sum can go into the pension.

rows.name: Cuts in a slump
rows.what: After a set number of months below the glidepath, income is cut by a set share (half the cut for the first months, the whole cut if it lasts), the cash buffer is kept, and missed income is made up later.
rows.whereV6: Stress and Decision → Settings → Protection (index.html:3584-3611; ProtectionStrategy.js)
rows.note: V7's answers run with cuts off (save-as-plan.md §C.3).

rows.name: Emergency reserve ("Break Glass HODL")
rows.what: A reserve touched only when the plan would otherwise fail.
rows.note: No test plan uses it yet (square-one-audit.md §4).

rows.name: Pots & Valves
rows.what: One flexible portfolio in three pots; rules decide which pot pays each month, with floors that run down over the plan and cuts in a slump.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → Income strategy; Strategies → Pots & Valves
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words. V7's answers draw this way today, with the cuts off.

rows.name: Buckets in order
rows.what: Cash pays first, then bonds, then shares; surplus refills from above when it is more than a set band over its path. Dials: the band, and the pension and ISA totals.
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Ladder & Ratchet
rows.what: Buys index-linked gilts for the first years of income and rides the rest in shares, selling only when shares are well above their path or on a calendar. Dials: years bought, the income bolted on, the trigger, the band, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Bridge & engine
rows.what: Every year to the bridge age (usually the State Pension) bought now, cash first then one gilt a year; the rest rides in shares untouched, then pays by withdrawals. Dials: the bridge age, years in cash, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.whereV6: Income strategy: Bridge & engine; Your pot (index.html:3166-3169)
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Floor & Flex
rows.what: Buys the essentials as a floor to an age with gilts; the rest is a flex sleeve paying a set share each year; booms can extend or raise the floor. Dials: essentials, the floor's end age, the sleeve rate, the treats rule, the ratchet, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words. V7 never fills the essentials from the budget (owner, 1 Oct 2026).

rows.name: Floor the schedule
rows.what: Buys the whole income shape, year by year, with index-linked gilts. Dials: the pension and ISA totals.
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Floor to an age, then decide
rows.what: Buys the income shape to an age with gilts and leaves the decision about the years after it for later. After a rotation is carried out the plan moves here, keeping a record of the income it sold (the borrowed floor) and what it would cost today to buy back. Dials: the age, the borrowed floor, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.whereV6: Income strategy: Floor to an age; Your pot (index.html:3165)
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Full index-linked gilt ladder
rows.what: Every year of the income shape bought with index-linked gilts, with the first years from cash. Dials: years from cash, the pension cash to the first April, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.whereV6: Income strategy: Full index-linked gilt ladder (index.html:3184-3192)
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Gilt ladder + rotation
rows.what: The full ladder, plus one agreed escape: if shares fall 30% below their high, the rungs beyond an age are sold to buy them cheap. Dials: years from cash, pension cash to April, the age kept to, the trigger and when it disarms, the pension and ISA totals.
rows.whereV6: Income strategy: Gilt ladder + rotation (index.html:3186-3189; strategies/GiltRotation.js)
rows.note: E's "compare" step; E's answer contract is not written yet (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6). Owner's decision pending: all nine answer in V7's words.

rows.name: Choose the plan's strategy; switch and come back
rows.what: Picks one strategy for the plan; switching puts each strategy's own inputs away and brings them back when you return.
rows.note: E's "mix" and "compare" steps.

rows.name: What a ladder or floor costs today, against your pot
rows.what: As the dials change: the cost of the gilts at today's real yields, what is left for shares, the first year's treats, and an illustrative ladder, or "not affordable".
rows.note: Part of each strategy's dials in E's "compare" step; no V7 design draws it.

rows.name: Compare all nine on your plan
rows.what: Ranks the strategies on your plan by a score, paid in full, coverage and the worst 12 months.
rows.note: Owner's decision pending: one kind of verdict ("lasts in 9 futures out of 10") for all nine (square-one-audit.md §6 question 2).

rows.name: A page for each strategy
rows.what: For each strategy: how the machine works, its dials, three real starts in history, and how it fails.
rows.note: E's outline names "compare" but no V7 design draws a page per strategy.

rows.name: Try this strategy in a copy of the plan
rows.what: Makes a copy of the plan on another strategy, with the pot totals carried over; the original is untouched.
rows.whereV6: "Try this strategy in a COPY of this plan" (index.html:3216-3217, 9707-9727)
rows.note: "Keep a try-a-change result as a separate plan".

rows.name: Gilt ladders explained, with a worked example
rows.what: What a gilt ladder is and what one costs today, for an amount and a number of years.
rows.whereV6: Strategies → Gilt ladders explained; Stress → Drawdown (index.html:2904-2916)
rows.note: E's "move" step.

rows.name: Gilt order sheet
rows.what: Which gilts to buy and how many (SEDOLs and nominal amounts), priced at the latest prices.
rows.whereV6: Strategy pages; gilt ladder pricing (index.html:6203-6250; GiltLadderPlan.js, LinkerUniverse.js)
rows.note: E's "move" step.

rows.name: Rotation watch and ticket
rows.what: For gilt ladder + rotation: how far shares are below their high, the ticket to act on when the trigger fires, and the guided switch that sells the block, buys shares and records the income sold.
rows.note: The locked rail's "move" station.

rows.name: Assumptions and data
rows.what: Where every figure comes from: the return history, inflation, gilt prices, and what is assumed.
rows.note: The trust pages (product-plan.md); V7 already says what each answer assumed (src/v7/components/Assumed.jsx).

rows.name: Monte Carlo: a thousand futures
rows.what: Runs the plan through 1,000 simulated futures and shows how often it lasts, with cones of income and wealth.
rows.note: E's "answer" step. V7's answers already run futures (src/answers/shared/futures.js) on the 9-in-10 bar.

rows.name: Every start year in history
rows.what: Runs the plan from every start year in the record and shows the worst sequences.
rows.note: E's "answer" step: "Does it come through the bad times?"

rows.name: Named stress scenarios
rows.what: Runs the plan through named crashes and bad decades.
rows.note: E's "answer" step.

rows.name: Try a strategy, never saved
rows.what: A what-if on any strategy, pot, ISA, income, years and cuts, run without changing the plan (works on a locked plan too); "Use this strategy for my plan" adopts it on an unlocked one.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Monte Carlo → Try a strategy (index.html:2818-2836)
rows.note: "Test the plan: try-only". V7's answers have Try a change (src/v7/components/TryAChange.jsx), and with a spending shape "Try it the same every year" and "Put back my steps by age" (today's "Income: … A flat amount").

rows.name: "What is this doing?"
rows.what: A plain explanation beside each test of what it runs and what its figures mean.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Monte Carlo, Historical, Scenarios: "What is this doing?" (openStressExplainer)
rows.note: V7 says what each answer assumed (src/v7/components/Assumed.jsx); an explanation of each test needs E.

rows.name: Compare allocations and apply the best split
rows.what: Searches the share, bond and cash split for Pots & Valves and offers to apply it.

rows.name: Drawdown schedule and the ISA bridge table
rows.what: Year by year: what is drawn from the pension and ISA, tax, and what is left; for a bought strategy its own schedule (income middle and 1 in 10).
rows.note: A's "What pays the bills before my State Pension starts?" (rail-screens-language.md §1.5) is a summary, not built.

rows.name: The glidepath picture
rows.what: Draws the pots' floors running down over the plan at an assumed inflation.

rows.name: Lock the plan and make the plan document
rows.what: Freezes the settings of both tools and writes the plan as committed; the first Decision record also locks it.
rows.whereV6: Stress → Settings → "Lock plan & create the plan document" (index.html:3636, 8510-8541; PlanLock.js)
rows.note: E's "lock" step; A and B (and later D) end with "Lock this plan?" (square-one-audit.md §5 item 5).

rows.name: Unlock to change the plan
rows.what: Unlocking keeps the plan document as a past version (last ten) and counts the unlocks.
rows.note: "Unlock to change the plan" keeps the document as a past version.

rows.name: The plan document
rows.what: The plan as committed: timeline, steps, the strategy's verdict, pots and assumptions; printed or saved as a PDF; refreshed on demand.
rows.note: The "Your plan" station reads the document only, never live settings. A plan locked while saving from 6.22.0 holds a version 3 saving path drawn on V7's saving-years engine (SavingPath.js): 1,000 futures, pension and ISA, the middle line and the 1-in-10 bad and good lines.

rows.name: The ladder card
rows.what: For a locked gilt plan: what arrives when, what has been bought, and what the same gilts would cost today, as a comparison only.
rows.note: The "Your plan" and "Moving to your plan's mix" stations ("6 of 18 gilts bought").

rows.name: The plan of record
rows.what: The drawdown and glidepath projection frozen when the Decision plan locked: a yardstick that does not move.
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: Where you are
rows.what: Reads the recorded months against the document: took this, the plan said that.
rows.note: The "Where you are" station.

rows.name: Arrival check
rows.what: The first month after a plan locked while saving reaches its stop: your pot against the plan's, then carry on or unlock and plan again.
rows.note: P.arrived. From 6.22.0 today's planner reads the arrival with the saver's reading (SaverReading.js): the pot at the first month after the stop against the locked path's middle line, in the path's own pounds, pension and ISA on a path drawn from 6.22.0.

rows.name: "Saved by a newer version"
rows.what: A plan saved by a newer version of the app is shown read-only, with a reload button.
rows.note: P.readonly.

rows.name: Nothing changes a locked plan
rows.what: Every button that writes settings refuses on a locked plan and says where the unlock is; records, holdings and the budget stay editable.
rows.note: "What a locked plan can and cannot do on the rail".

rows.name: Record a month
rows.what: This month's fund values (by bucket, or fund by fund), the ISA, diversifiers, the taxable account and its cost; "paid this month already".
rows.note: The "This month" station. Owner's decision pending: 7.0 may ship with Month by month on today's screen (square-one-audit.md §6 question 3).

rows.name: What to draw and from where
rows.what: The month's recommendation: how much, from which pot, what to sell or rebalance, the tax summary.

rows.name: How often you draw
rows.what: Monthly, quarterly or a year at a time.
rows.whereV6: Decision → Monthly Entry: How often you draw (index.html:2301-2310, 5960-5970)

rows.name: History, plan against actual
rows.what: Every recorded month by tax year, against the plan; delete a year or everything.
rows.note: The "Where you are" station.

rows.name: A spreadsheet per tax year, and PDFs
rows.what: Downloads each tax year's records and prints the documents.
rows.note: Carried over with Month by month (square-one-audit.md §4).

rows.name: Set up a tax year
rows.what: Each April: the bands, last year's price rise, other income, the ISA to use, the tax-efficiency choice, income and tax already this year, the start month and the confirmed target; edit a year or set it up again.
rows.note: P.taxyear: "Next: set up the {2027/28} tax year."

rows.name: Copy settings between the two tools
rows.what: "Copy from Decision Tool" seeds the Stress tester from the committed plan; "Use ALL Stress settings" or "Copy target amount only" goes the other way.
rows.reason: V7 keeps one plan and tries changes without saving them (rail-screens-language.md §1.6), so there are no two tools to copy between: every figure the copy carried is in the one plan.

rows.name: Where a copy came from
rows.what: Which tool a settings copy came from, when, and a fingerprint of the source (for a "changed since you copied" note).
rows.reason: Belongs to "Copy settings between the two tools" (retired with it, once the owner agrees); old plans keep these keys untouched.

rows.name: What you pay in, and your employer
rows.what: What you pay each month from take-home, and what your employer adds.
rows.note: One figure that lands in the pension, or split into your part and your employer's.

rows.name: What goes into ISAs and savings each month
rows.what: A monthly amount into ISAs and other savings, from take-home pay (no tax relief), raised each year like the pension payments; it counts in the pots at retirement, the age spin and a plan locked while saving.
rows.whereV6: Accumulation → Contributions → Into ISAs and savings (index.html #acIsaMonthly, 6.22.0)
rows.note: V7 asked for it first ("savingsIn"); a plan made from an answer now keeps it in the planner's box.

rows.name: How tax relief works, and your salary
rows.what: Relief at source, net pay or salary sacrifice, with your salary, so the higher-rate reclaim and the NI saving are shown.
rows.whereV6: Accumulation → How relief works; Salary (index.html:3682-3692; AccumulationEngine.contributionBreakdown)
rows.note: V7 takes what lands in the pension, the tax added back included; it does not ask how relief is given.

rows.name: Raise payments by a % a year
rows.what: Payments rise by a set percentage each year.

rows.name: Age, retiring age, pension today
rows.what: The Accumulation planner's own age, retirement age and pot today.

rows.name: The Accumulation planner's part of the plan
rows.what: Where the saving years' settings are kept on the plan.
rows.note: A plan made from a V7 answer with money still going in carries it.

rows.name: Projection to the retirement age
rows.what: The pot at each age at 2%, 5% and 8%, with what was paid in.
rows.note: Replaced, better: the saving-years engine with a middling and a bad case.

rows.name: A projection at your own holdings' mix
rows.what: A fourth projection line at the expected return of what you hold, net of its costs.
rows.note: V7 projects at a risk level while saving (savingRisk).

rows.name: When could I retire?
rows.what: Which age clears the bar for an income wanted, if saving carries on.
rows.note: A's every-age table, on the saving-years engine.

rows.name: Am I on course?
rows.what: The pot needed for the plan's target and whether the saving gets there.
rows.whereV6: Accumulation → Am I on course? (index.html "Am I on course?"; src/services/OnCourse.js, src/ui/accumulationProjection.js)
rows.note: B, with the monthly amount that gets there and the options if it does not fit. One bar everywhere from 6.22.0: on course = lasts in 9 futures out of 10 (OnCourse.ON_COURSE_SHARE = V7's BAND.careful).

rows.name: Payment warnings
rows.what: Warns when payments pass the annual allowance, the £10,000 limit after drawing, or relevant earnings.
rows.note: Annual allowance, the £10,000 limit, the ISA allowance, and paying in past 75.

rows.name: Record this month's pot
rows.what: One line a month while saving (pension, ISA, taxable), read against the locked plan's saving path.
rows.note: A saver's station, "This month's pot" (square-one-audit.md §5 item 4). The reading was fixed first (item 2, 6.22.0): read at the record's month, from the path's own start, in the path's pounds; plans locked from 6.22.0 draw the path on V7's saving-years engine (pension and ISA, 1-in-10 lines; src/services/SavingPath.js, SaverReading.js).

rows.name: What you hold
rows.what: One record of what you actually hold, line by line by wrapper (pension, ISA, taxable, cash): ticker, name, SEDOL, units, value, cost, payments, sub-class, kind, date; typed or pasted from a platform; never the funds a strategy is tested on.
rows.whereV6: Transition → What you hold; Accumulation → Record what I hold (TransitionView.js:41-89; HoldingsRecord.js, HoldingsPaste.js)
rows.note: E's "hold" step and the locked rail's "What you hold" station (§1.6). The "Holdings and the move" sub-plan is not written (square-one-audit.md §5 item 6).

rows.name: Moving to the plan's mix
rows.what: The buy and sell list, the cash to hold, the schedule and the tick-offs as each move is placed.
rows.note: E's "move" step, which says on its face that it is optional and what skipping it costs.

rows.name: The partner's linked plan
rows.what: Links this plan to the partner's own plan, or creates theirs and switches to it.
rows.note: Better: a couple's figures on the first screen; saving makes the two linked plans.

rows.name: Will the money last for both of us?
rows.what: Runs the two plans together.
rows.note: Every V7 answer is the household's; 6.20.0 adds couples who stop in different years.

rows.name: Survivor check
rows.what: What happens to the money if one of you dies.
rows.note: Gets a station at the switch (square-one-audit.md §5 item 9); "today's planner keeps them" until then (answer-D.md §8).

rows.name: Care-cost check
rows.what: Whether the money stands a spell of care costs for one of you.
rows.note: Gets a station at the switch (square-one-audit.md §5 item 9).

rows.name: Your plans: switch, new, duplicate, rename
rows.what: A menu of plans: open one, start a new one, duplicate one, rename it and describe it.
rows.note: Plan menu in V7's shell (square-one-audit.md §5 item 9).

rows.name: Download a plan
rows.what: Saves a copy of the plan (JSON) on your own computer.
rows.note: Plan menu in V7's shell.

rows.name: Save a V7 answer as a new plan
rows.what: A V7 answer becomes a named plan in today's planner; a couple's becomes two linked plans; the answer it came from is kept with it.

rows.name: What's new
rows.what: A once-only pop-up for each minor release, and every release listed on a page.
rows.note: What's new in V7's shell (square-one-audit.md §5 item 9).

rows.name: Sign in and out
rows.what: Email and password or Google, a verified email, and signing out after an hour idle across tabs.
rows.note: Must exist in V7 at the switch (data protection; square-one-audit.md §4).

rows.name: Delete the account, or reset
rows.what: Deletes the account and every plan, or deletes all data and starts again.
rows.note: Must exist in V7 at the switch (data protection).

rows.name: Reset a tool's settings to the defaults
rows.what: Puts the Stress tester's or the Decision tool's settings back to the defaults (refused on a locked plan).
rows.whereV6: Stress and Decision → Settings → Reset to Defaults

rows.name: Which tools a plan shows
rows.what: Turns tools on or off for a plan, with a short wizard when a tool is added.
rows.reason: V7 has no tool tabs: the rail shows the steps the plan's stage needs, so there is nothing to switch on or off.

rows.name: Administration
rows.what: The owner's panel: the fund catalogue, the typical amounts, the queue of unknown tickers.
rows.note: Owner only; could stay on the previous version's page.

rows.name: The plan's own fields
rows.what: The plan's id, when it was made and last changed.
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: The parts a plan is kept in
rows.what: The Stress tester's, the Decision tool's and the Budget's parts of a plan.
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: The plan's strategy block
rows.what: Which strategy the plan runs, with its dials, when it was chosen and the engine version.
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: Settings have been saved once
rows.what: Marks a plan whose settings have been through Settings at least once, so the tool opens straight away.
rows.note: Carried as stored: V7 reads and writes the same saved plan (architecture.md §3.9: no change to the shape of saved plans at 7.0).

rows.name: The old "Declining with age" spending profile
rows.what: A spending profile that drifted down with age, applied on top of the income steps.
rows.reason: Retired in 6.2.1: "Declining with age" became a slope on the income steps, with the same figures; old plans are folded in when opened. The taper itself is kept: in V7 it is the preset "Slowly less" (src/answers/shared/shape.js slowlyLess, today's smileToSteps).

rows.name: Old names of the three pot floors
rows.what: The names the shares, bonds and cash floors had before they were renamed.
rows.reason: Renamed before 6.15.0 to equityMin, bondMin and cashTarget; kept beside the new names on old plans and read only to fill a missing new one.

rows.name: Copies under dotted names
rows.what: Copies of a plan's parts that an old storage fault wrote under names with dots in them.
rows.reason: Never a setting: copies a storage fault wrote, folded back into the plan when it is opened.

rows.name: riskMode on the example plan
rows.what: A field written only by the guest example plan.
rows.reason: Read by nothing in today's app; the example plan's allocMode carries the same thing.

rows.name: The Decision tool's old start date
rows.what: An early Decision field for when the plan started, always empty.
rows.reason: Read by nothing; the plan's start is its first tax year (design/settings-model.md lists it as a dead field).
